title: Youth justice programs, grantee by grantee
question: For each Justice Services program page saved, what was granted and spent, how many young people took part and what did a day of service cost?
finding: 12 of the 33 Justice Services programs were saved as program pages (both years); they account for $5.4 million of spending in 2024-25 and $5.4 million in 2025-26. 4 program-years left 15% or more of the grant unspent. Highest spending per participant: Catholic Charities CYO of the Archdiocese of San Francisco, Boys Home Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (2025-26): $794,317 for 10 participants, $79,432 each.
how: Every program page in the folder was read: grant and expenditures, sites, service dates, participants and participant service days from the Activities panel, and the average hours line. Cost per day is expenditures over participant service days; per participant is expenditures over participants (blank where the page reports only aggregate days).
limits: Only 12 of 33 programs were saved, so totals here are partial. Residential and custody programs serve few young people intensively, so high cost per participant is expected there; the department's pages give no reason for unspent grant. Participant counts leave out young people reported in aggregate.
